title.narrative: Ai transformation, human rights, data governance and privacy in Ghana

description.narrative: Ghana recently launched a National AI Strategy, a comprehensive roadmap enabling the country to capitalise on the socio-economic benefits of AI while mitigating its hazards. The strategy envisages a transformed society by 2035, where AI will advance the potential of our people, government, businesses and systems, achieving inclusive social and economic transformation. Central to the implementation of the AI strategy is the role of civil servants in delivering essential services that protect public goods, human rights, and socio-economic development. While AI and digital technologies can improve government operations, they also introduce risks relating to bias, transparency and ethics. This makes the use of human rights-based AI essential for sustaining public trust and development. Therefore, strengthening the capacity of the public sector is crucial for AI transformation.
